title: Oct 15 Results + Oct 16 Preview: Split Decision, Back to the Lab
summary: Went 1-1 on Oct 15. Guardians delivered, Dodgers didn't. Rays-Guardians rematch up next.

content.value:
## Oct 15 Recap: Even Money

From the mound, you learn quick that not every pitch works. Today was one of those days—went 1-1, splitting the slate at 50%. The Guardians pick cashed at 52%, but the Dodgers let us down at 61% confidence. That's baseball. You trust your stuff, accept the results, and make adjustments.

## What Worked, What Didn't

**Guardians (✓)**: Cleveland came through at home, exactly as projected. A narrow 52% edge, but when you're working the corners, you take those tight margins. The home park advantage and bullpen depth played out.

**Dodgers (✗)**: This one stings. 61% confidence should hold more often than not, but the Brewers had other plans. Sometimes the opposing lineup just sees the ball better than expected. You tip your cap and move on.

## Oct 16 Preview: Rays-Guardians Rematch

Here's where it gets interesting. Same teams, different day. Nick Martinez takes the ball for Tampa Bay against Shawn Armstrong for Cleveland. The model's flipping the script—now favoring the Rays at 54% after backing the Guardians yesterday.

content.value:
## Pitcher's Perspective: Martinez vs Armstrong

Nick Martinez brings versatility to the bump—he can start, he can relieve, and he's seen every role in the book. That experience matters in October. Armstrong's typically a reliever making a spot start situation, which changes the dynamic completely.

From a pitcher's view, when you're facing a guy out of his normal routine, you can exploit the rhythm issue. Martinez has better command of his arsenal in a traditional starter's role. Armstrong's effective in short bursts, but stretching him out is a different animal.

The Rays at 54% feels right. It's essentially a coin flip with a slight edge based on the pitching matchup. In playoff baseball, I'll take the experienced starter over the bullpen arm every time.

## The Bottom Line

Oct 15 was a wash—one hit, one miss. That's the grind. Oct 16 brings a rematch with better pitching circumstances for Tampa Bay. Trust the process, trust the arm talent, and let's get back over .500.

Keep grinding. See you after first pitch.
